explanation: Archaea are known to thrive in harsh environments. Methanogens live in anaerobic marshes and produce methane from hydrogen gas and carbon dioxide. Halophiles reside in salty lakes and require high salt concentrations for growth. Thermoacidophiles inhabit hot sulfur springs and thermal vents, where they reduce sulfides and survive best at low pH and temperatures above 80°C. Their plasma membranes contain unusual lipids that convey tolerance to these high temperatures.

questions.q: What type of Archaea lives in anaerobic marshes and produces methane gas?
questions.exp: The notes state that methanogens live in anaerobic marshes and 'Produce methane from hydrogen gas and carbon dioxide'.

questions.q: What structural feature allows thermoacidophiles to tolerate temperatures above 80°C?
opts: An outer cell wall containing peptidoglycan
questions.exp: According to the notes, their 'Plasma membranes contain unusual lipids convey tolerance of high temperatures'.
